I built the to-do service, and all 8 end-to-end tests pass. They start the real server as a subprocess, use real HTTP, and restart it on the same db file. `run_guard.py` was blocked by the permission layer, so this run was unguarded. **Acceptance checks** (I derived these from your request):

| Criterion | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /users` returns 201 with id and token | `test_user_and_list_flow`, `test_users_post_without_body` | ran, passed |
| `POST /lists` returns 201 with id; `GET /lists` and `GET /lists/ID` work for the owner | `test_user_and_list_flow` | ran, passed |
| A list is visible only to its owner; another user gets 404 on `GET /lists/ID` and an empty list on `GET /lists` | `test_isolation` | ran, passed |
| A missing or bogus token gets 401 on all three authenticated routes | `test_unauthorized` | ran, passed |
| Data survives a restart on the same `--db` path | `test_persistence_across_restart` | ran, passed |
| Bad titles or malformed bodies get 400; a SQL-injection title is stored as plain text | `test_bad_input`, `test_injection_title_is_inert` | ran, passed |
| The plaintext token is not in the db file | `test_token_not_stored_plaintext` | ran, passed |

I ran them with `py -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Bash and PowerShell here don't have `python` on PATH; `py` is Python 3.12.10.

**Decisions** (recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`):
- **Storage:** SQLite through the standard library, in one file given by `--db`. A `Store` class owns all state, and every list query is filtered by owner.
- **Tokens:** random 32-byte bearer tokens. Only the SHA-256 hash is stored.
- **Responses:** another user's list returns 404, the same as a missing one. List items are `{"id","title"}`, with a title of 1–500 characters.
- **Network:** it binds to 127.0.0.1 only, with no TLS and no rate limit, since deployment was excluded.

**Limits:**
- `POST /users` is open and unthrottled, so anyone who can reach the server can create accounts.
- Tokens have no expiry or revocation.
- I didn't run `check_stack.py` or a security scan; the stack was fixed by your constraints, and I skipped the layer-by-layer stack flow.
